context: The integer array is nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], with indices 0 through 3. The target sum is target = 13.

Find two distinct positions whose elements sum to target and return their indices. The same position cannot be used twice. The brute-force method checks pairs with nested loops, using i as the outer index and j as the inner index, where j > i.
description: The four-by-four matrix at the bottom has row and column headers 2, 7, 11, and 15. Its six candidate sums appear only above the main diagonal. This excludes pairing a position with itself on the diagonal and repeating a pair in reverse order below it. The elements and candidate sums in the table come from the matrix. Each index pair uses the elements' zero-based positions in the input, and each addition combines its row and column headers.

The cell at row 0 (element 2) and column 2 (element 11) highlights 13 in blue-violet. The code checks pairs from left to right. With i = 0 (element 2) fixed, the inner loop first computes 2 + 7 = 9, then 2 + 11 = 13. This matches the target, so the code immediately returns [0, 2]. The figure includes the other sums to show all possible pairs. The code does not compute the remaining sums after a match.

frames.explanation: The nested loops take O(n²) time and use O(1) auxiliary space, trading time for space.
